packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

No proposed identification or reading of this text was visible in my context.
Beyond the brief: I computed content bounding boxes of the tiles with a small Pillow script (kept in a session temp folder, not in the packet) and viewed crops of each tile's content area (crop-NNN.jpg = crop of image-NNN.jpg) instead of the whole mostly-grey tile. Line numbers below are counted from the top of the tile's written area.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overview image-001; other overviews at 006, 011, 016, 021, 026, 031, 034, 037, 042 not yet viewed when this was written)
- image-001 shows four separate small parchment strips on a grey ground, each with a modern pencil shelfmark "Stams, STA, Frg. 165/1 - 21r", "22r", "23r", "24r". These are binding strips (cut horizontally), each holding about 4 lines of text, with no full column width or margins preserved except a left margin on 21r and 23r. Black rectangles on 21r/22r are masking/mounting patches (or holes backed with dark paper).
- Script: a late-medieval cursive (gothic cursiva) book hand, single column, brown ink, long descenders on s/f, heavy abbreviation. No rubrics or initials seen on these strips.
- Tile mapping: each overview has 4 native tiles in quadrant order (TL, TR, BL, BR), e.g. 002=21r, 003=22r, 004=23r, 005=24r.

==== SUMMARY / LIMITATIONS ====
- Material: 20 small horizontal parchment strips (pencil "Stams, STA, Frg. 165/1 - 21r ... 40v"), each with 1-5 lines, cut from one or more documents (binding strips). Many strips keep a margin on one side (left on recto, right on verso, consistent with the same strip), and several (26, 28, 29, 31 and 34) are mostly blank below 1-2 lines, which suggests lower margins/ends of documents. I did not try to put the strips in order.
- Script: one (or very similar) late-medieval documentary cursive in brown ink, heavy abbreviation, virgulae (/) used as punctuation, flourished capitals (E, D, C, V/M) inside lines, long hairline flourishes into the margin. Some features (horizontal pen lines, paraph-like scrawls, a possible "Concor[..]" note, "...facta est cum Registro") look like chancery/notarial practice. Observation only.
- Content (visible words only, no identification): ecclesiastical-legal vocabulary - "reformationis ecclesie et correctionis", "decanum ecclesie sancti Johannis in ...", "herbipolen-", "sacri concilii Basilien-", "in dicto sacro concilio", "citatus ... prima die iuridica", "et contemptores fuerint pronun|ciare volumus ipso facto", "absencia non obstante / Datum Basilee in ambitu ... Anno domini Millesimo", "mille marcharum argenti", "sacri Ordinis C...", "Cuius tenor sequitur", "infrascripti tenor sequitur", "Ita tamen quod nullus ex transgressoribus", "ex superhabundanti ca(u)-". Two strips (29r and 31r) carry the same wording ("dicto? ... non comparuerit nisi ... in aliquo satisfacere ...") with different line breaks, i.e. two copies of one formula.
- 33v: a marginal note with a looped sign plus "31" ("[?]431" or "y31"), unclear whether a year.
- Unread: strip 34v (appears blank on overview image-034, not inspected at tile level); faint traces near the lower left of 26r and below line 2 of 29r; strip 34r is nearly illegible (faded) - UV/multispectral imaging suggested.
- Wasted views: crop-015.jpg (empty grey area, my cropping error) and the lower part of crop-012.jpg/crop-017.jpg missed the first line, so I made top crops crop-012b.jpg/crop-017b.jpg. No image was removed from my context by the image limit; I did not stop on the limit.
- Readings marked "?" are uncertain; many words are letter-by-letter guesses. This is an unverified image reading.
